title: 147. Quantitative Relationships & Measurement: Interpreting Percentage-Based Charts
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.learningObjective: Determine the combined percentage of two sectors in a pie chart.
questions.question: A pie chart shows four categories: A \(40\%\), B \(25\%\), C \(20\%\), and D \(15\%\). What is the combined percentage for categories A and B?
questions.explanation: The combined percentage for categories A and B is \(40\%+25\%=65\%\). Therefore, the correct value is \(65\%\). Option A is too small because \(40\%+20\%=60\%\), which combines A and C instead.
questions.hint: Identify which category and which total the percentage refers to.

questions.concept: Percentage of Total in a Bar Chart
questions.learningObjective: Calculate a category amount from its percentage in a bar chart.
questions.question: A bar chart shows monthly sales as percentages of a first-quarter total: January \(20\%\), February \(30\%\), and March \(50\%\). If the total first-quarter sales are \(200\text{ units}\), how many units were sold in March?
questions.explanation: March accounts for \(50\%\) of the total. Since \(50\%\) of \(200\) is \(0.50\times 200=100\), the number of units sold in March is \(100\). The alternative treats the numerical percentage \(50\) as a unit count instead of finding half of the total.
questions.hint: Distinguish a known part from the whole chart total.

questions.concept: Reading Percentage from a Stacked Bar Chart
questions.learningObjective: Calculate a subgroup count from a percentage in a stacked bar chart.
questions.question: A stacked bar chart shows that \(45\%\) of students prefer tea, \(35\%\) prefer coffee, and \(20\%\) prefer juice. If \(400\) students were surveyed, how many prefer coffee?
questions.explanation: Coffee represents \(35\%\) of the surveyed students: \(0.35\times 400=140\). The alternative counts the students who do not prefer coffee: \(400-140=260\).
questions.hint: Apply the category's percentage to the total number of students surveyed.

questions.concept: Identifying Sectors with a Given Combined Percentage
questions.learningObjective: Identify two pie-chart sectors whose combined percentage equals a stated value.
questions.question: A pie chart shows housing \(30\%\), food \(25\%\), transport \(15\%\), and other \(30\%\). Which of the following pairs of categories accounts for exactly \(55\%\)?
questions.explanation: Housing is \(30\%\) and food is \(25\%\), so their combined percentage is \(30\%+25\%=55\%\). Housing and other would give \(30\%+30\%=60\%\). Therefore, the correct pair is housing and food.
questions.hint: Add the percentages of the two sectors in each pair and compare each sum with the target percentage.

questions.concept: Finding Total from a Pie Chart Percentage
questions.learningObjective: Determine total annual sales from a sector percentage and value.
questions.question: In a pie chart of annual sales, third-quarter sales are \(25\%\) of the total and equal \(50{,}000\text{ yuan}\). What are the total annual sales?
questions.explanation: The known sales are one quarter of the total, so the total is \(\frac{50{,}000}{0.25}=200{,}000\text{ yuan}\). The alternative multiplies the known part by its fraction: \(50{,}000\times 0.25=12{,}500\text{ yuan}\), instead of recovering the whole.
questions.hint: Distinguish a known part from the whole chart total.

questions.concept: Calculating a Count from a Percentage Chart
questions.learningObjective: Determine the number of participants corresponding to a given percentage.
questions.question: A percentage chart shows that \(65\%\) of \(80\) participants chose the first proposal. How many participants chose the first proposal?
questions.explanation: The count is \(0.65\times 80=52\) participants. The alternative counts the participants who did not choose the first proposal: \(80-52=28\).
questions.hint: Convert the percentage to a decimal and apply it to the total number of participants.

questions.concept: Finding Total from a Pie Chart Sector Value
questions.learningObjective: Determine total value from a \(50\%\) sector value.
questions.question: In a circle graph, sector Z represents \(50\%\) of the total and has a value of \(120\text{ units}\). What is the total value?
questions.explanation: The given sector is half the total, so the total is \(\frac{120}{0.50}=240\text{ units}\). The alternative halves the known part again: \(120\times 0.50=60\), rather than doubling it to recover the whole.
questions.hint: Identify which category and which total the percentage refers to.

questions.learningObjective: Calculate percentage increase between two chart values.
questions.question: A bar chart shows a value increasing from \(120\) in \(2020\) to \(150\) in \(2021\). What is the percentage increase?
questions.explanation: The increase is \(150-120=30\). Use the original value as the base: \(\frac{30}{120}\times 100\%=25\%\). The alternative \(20\%\) divides by the final value \(150\).
questions.hint: Use the original chart value as the base for a relative change.

questions.concept: Using a Pie Chart to Find Another Sector Value
questions.learningObjective: Determine a sector value from another sector's percentage and value.
questions.question: A pie chart shows A \(30\%\), B \(45\%\), and C \(25\%\). If sector B represents \(90\text{ units}\), what does sector C represent?
questions.explanation: Sector B is \(45\%\) of the total. Since \(45\%\) of the total is \(90\), the total is \(90\div 0.45=200\). Sector C is \(25\%\) of the total, so it represents \(0.25\times 200=50\text{ units}\). The alternative copies the numerical percentage for sector B, \(45\), as sector C's unit count.
questions.hint: Use the sector with a known value to recover the chart total first.

questions.concept: Successive Percentage Changes from Chart Data
questions.learningObjective: Calculate final revenue after a percentage increase and a percentage decrease shown in a chart.
questions.question: A revenue chart shows \(2022\) revenue of \(500{,}000\text{ yuan}\). In \(2023\), revenue increased by \(20\%\). In \(2024\), revenue decreased by \(10\%\) from \(2023\). What is the \(2024\) revenue?
questions.explanation: After a \(20\%\) increase, the \(2023\) revenue is \(500{,}000\times 1.20=600{,}000\text{ yuan}\). After a \(10\%\) decrease from \(2023\), the \(2024\) revenue is \(600{,}000\times 0.90=540{,}000\text{ yuan}\). Therefore, the correct value is \(540{,}000\text{ yuan}\). Option B incorrectly subtracts \(10\%\) of the original \(2022\) revenue.
questions.hint: Identify which category and which total the percentage refers to.
